messages.author: 8ae1efaa2cf53fab
messages.subject: Re: R and Aroma_Affymetrix course?
parts:
Hi Myriam

I don't know about aroma.affymetrix courses but for R your best place
to start, as a biologist, is at the Bioconductor project. Their
introductory page spells out exactly the steps that you should follow:
http://www.bioconductor.org/GettingStarted

Most of the older workshops are listed (http://www.bioconductor.org/
workshops), and there you can obtain test data and code to try our the
different packages and get a better feeling for R.

Otherwise there are some excellent introductory guides to R on the
internet, e.g.
http://www.ats.ucla.edu/stat/r/sk/
http://disinterested.googlepages.com/GettingStartedWithR.pdf

Good luck!

Lavinia.

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: R and Aroma_Affymetrix course?
parts:
Hi,

except from what Lavinia already said, I can only say that there are
no workshops planned on aroma.* analysis.

For aroma.*, the best you have now is the online vignettes and labs;

(a) http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/use-cases
(b) http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/training-lab-sessions

I encourage anyone who gives private crash courses on aroma.* to share
their slides/handouts to be added on the site.

/Henrik
